taxonomy.note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO; native range is south Texas to northeastern Mexico. Passiflora bigelovii is a historical synonym.

evidence: Hays County — UT Plant Resources Center has a dedicated Hays Flora page for Passiflora tenuiloba and Purola Preserve natural flora lists it as naturally occurring.
Travis County — UT Plant Resources Center's Travis County Passifloraceae herbarium index includes Passiflora tenuiloba.
Val Verde County — the Amistad National Recreation Area vascular flora documents P. tenuiloba with multiple vouchers on trees, shrubs, rock outcrops, ledges and cliffs.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Broad Edwards Plateau occurrence is not converted into county proof; the PASS uses exact county flora/herbarium documentation.

morphology.look_here_first: Look at the leaf silhouette and petiole glands. Birdwing passionflower has a pair of cuplike glands at the petiole apex and extremely narrow, deeply divided 3–9-lobed leaves; the two lateral primary lobes are often long and winglike while the middle lobe is shorter or further divided.
diagnostic_traits: perennial prostrate or low-climbing vine with slender coiling tendrils
petiole glandular with paired saucer- or cup-shaped glands near the blade
leaf blades extremely variable but deeply 3–9-lobed
primary lobes narrow and acute; lateral lobes often long and spreading
primary lobes may themselves be lobed, creating a birdwing/handlike silhouette
petals absent; 6–10 green sepals and two whorls of corona filaments form the showy portion
ripe berries small, globose, dark blue to black

confusers.separator: P. lutea has glandless petioles and broad rounded 3-lobed leaves; P. tenuiloba has paired cuplike petiole glands and narrow deeply dissected lobes.

Both have petiole glands, but P. incarnata has much broader serrated 3-lobed leaves, huge purple/white flowers and large green-yellow maypops. P. tenuiloba has narrow entire lobes and tiny petal-less green flowers.
Another small green-flowered Central/West Texas passionflower. Use leaf architecture and gland characters; P. tenuiloba typically has the distinctive narrow deeply divided birdwing leaves.

diagnostic_roles: petiole apex macro showing paired cuplike glands
photo_verification.provenance_note: Because leaf shape varies even on one plant, the learner should show multiple mature leaf silhouettes plus the petiole-gland close-up.
